academy-story.text: Treat Academy instruction as lived dramatic action, not a lecture transcript. Let students interrupt, handle equipment, make plausible wrong assumptions, and solve concrete operational problems. Diagrams must exist inside the room and be readable through character interaction rather than replacing the comic page with an infographic.

corridor-physics.text: Corridors are physically safe three-dimensional low-tension volumes, not ocean channels or glowing hard tunnels. Show a surveyed spine between beacons with an approximately circular certified envelope whose usable diameter is about twice the beam of the largest ship the route is certified to carry. Outside the envelope, risk rises through reciprocal-field gradient, shear, phase and correction load rather than an invisible wall.

beacon-rules.text: A green beacon means local measurements support the certified safe envelope. Red means the route must not be relied on: either measured tension is outside limits or sensing is failed/insufficient. Sensor failure therefore defaults to red. Extreme tension can physically damage or shatter a beacon.

survey-culture.text: Survey work is empirical and repetitive: offset passes, repeated measurements, drift comparison, mass-envelope checks, timestamping and provenance. Fleet and private survey crews share technical craft even when their obligations and customers differ. Never portray route knowledge as mystical intuition.

color-grammar.text: Preserve Rex Fleet color grammar. Green belongs to the Verge and ordinary life sustained by public corridors. Fleet is blue/gold/white Crown stewardship. Shards are bright red. Survey craft are purple; blockade runners carry subtle cyan; maintenance/science/geology craft may use industrial yellow; Tempest is dark purple and gold; Crimson is deep institutional red with Fleet gold and must remain visibly distinct from bright-red Shard coding.
